# Omnivore - Universal Web Scraper & Code Extractor

Omnivore is a high-performance Rust CLI tool for web crawling, content extraction, and code analysis. It's designed to produce clean, structured output suitable for LLM consumption.

## Installation

```bash
cargo install omnivore-cli
# or
brew install omnivore
```

## Commands Overview

### 1. `omnivore crawl <URL>` - Web Crawling
Crawl websites and extract clean text content.

**Key Options:**
- `--stdout` - Output to stdout (for piping)
- `--format <FORMAT>` - Output format: json, markdown, csv, yaml, text
- `--depth <N>` - Maximum crawl depth (default: 5)
- `--workers <N>` - Parallel workers (default: 10)
- `--extract-tables` - Extract tables as CSV
- `--organize` - Create folder structure with separate files
- `--exclude-urls` - Remove URLs from output (cleaner for LLMs)
- `--ai <QUERY>` - Natural language extraction (requires OpenAI API)
- `--browser` - Use headless Chrome for JavaScript content

**Example Usage:**
```bash
# Basic crawl to JSON
omnivore crawl https://docs.example.com --format json -o docs.json

# Crawl to markdown for LLM consumption
omnivore crawl https://api.example.com --format markdown --stdout | llm

# Extract specific content with AI
omnivore crawl https://store.example.com --ai "get all product names and prices"

# Crawl with table extraction
omnivore crawl https://data.example.com --extract-tables --organize
```

**Output Structure (JSON):**
```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com",
  "pages": 10,
  "words": 5000,
  "duration_ms": 2500,
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "content": [
    {
      "url": "https://example.com/page1",
      "title": "Page Title",
      "text": "Clean extracted text content...",
      "words": 500,
      "links": ["https://example.com/related"]
    }
  ]
}
```

### 2. `omnivore git <SOURCE>` - Code Analysis
Extract and analyze code from Git repositories or local directories.

**Key Options:**
- `--stdout` - Output to stdout
- `--json` - Output as JSON format
- `--only <PATTERNS>` - Include only matching file patterns (comma-separated)
- `--exclude <PATTERNS>` - Exclude matching patterns
- `--depth <N>` - Clone depth for remote repos
- `--max-file-size <BYTES>` - Skip files larger than size

**Example Usage:**
```bash
# Analyze local repository
omnivore git . --stdout

# Analyze remote repository
omnivore git https://github.com/user/repo --output analysis.txt

# Extract only specific file types
omnivore git ./project --only "*.rs,*.toml" --stdout

# JSON output for programmatic use
omnivore git ./project --json --stdout
```

**Output Structure (JSON):**
```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "project_type": "Web Application",
    "description": "A Next.js project",
    "main_language": "TypeScript",
    "frameworks": ["Next.js", "React"],
    "build_tools": ["npm", "webpack"],
    "total_files": 50
  },
  "sections": [
    {
      "name": "Source Code",
      "description": "Main application source code",
      "files": [
        {
          "path": "src/index.ts",
          "content": "// file contents..."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### 3. `omnivore parse <FILE>` - HTML Parsing
Parse and extract content from local HTML files.

**Example:**
```bash
omnivore parse page.html -o parsed.json
```

### 4. `omnivore config [KEY] [VALUE]` - Configuration
Get or set configuration values.

**Available Keys:**
- `openai_api_key` - OpenAI API key for AI features
- `model` - AI model (gpt-4, gpt-3.5-turbo)
- `max_workers` - Default parallel workers
- `max_depth` - Default crawl depth
- `format` - Default output format
- `rate_limit` - Request delay in ms

**Example:**
```bash
omnivore config openai_api_key sk-xxx...
omnivore config model gpt-4
omnivore config  # Show all config
```

### 5. `omnivore setup` - Interactive Setup
Run interactive configuration wizard for API keys and settings.

### 6. `omnivore docs` - Documentation
Open documentation in browser.

## Output Formats

| Format | Best For | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `json` | APIs, programmatic use | Structured data with metadata |
| `markdown` | LLM consumption | Clean text with headers |
| `text` | Simple processing | Plain text output |
| `csv` | Spreadsheets | Tabular data |
| `yaml` | Config files | Human-readable structured |

## Tips for LLM Workflows

1. **Clean output for context:** Use `--exclude-urls --format markdown` for cleaner text
2. **Pipe directly to LLM:** `omnivore crawl URL --stdout --format text | llm`
3. **Extract code for analysis:** `omnivore git . --stdout | llm "explain this codebase"`
4. **Structured extraction:** Use `--ai "extract key points"` for targeted content

## Smart Filtering (git command)

The git command automatically excludes:
- Package managers (node_modules, vendor, __pycache__)
- Build outputs (dist, build, target, .next)
- Binary files and large models (*.pt, *.pkl)
- IDE configs (.idea, .vscode)
- Lock files and caches

Override with `--only` or `--include` flags.

## Environment Variables

- `OPENAI_API_KEY` - OpenAI API key
- `OMNIVORE_CONFIG_DIR` - Custom config directory
- `OMNIVORE_LOG_LEVEL` - Log level (debug, info, warn, error)

## Common Patterns

```bash
# Documentation to context
omnivore crawl https://docs.example.com -d 3 --format markdown -o docs.md

# Codebase summary for LLM
omnivore git . --stdout | head -1000 > context.txt

# API reference extraction
omnivore crawl https://api.example.com --ai "extract all endpoints with parameters"

# Multi-site crawl (bash)
for site in site1.com site2.com; do
  omnivore crawl "https://$site" -o "${site}.json"
done
```
